51136-nothing-but-the-best.creator: Unknown
51136-nothing-but-the-best.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. d just left, though he was pleased to note that Finlay's Lumber Co. It was proof that he had made the switch successfully. For some reason, Finlay never seemed to have established his business anywhere but in Charles Mead's world. There were similar changes in every world--some large changes, some small--but at least Hobson's Hill was always there, which was why he chose it as his jumping-off point.

arxiv-1905-13189.title: A Beginner’s Guide to Working with Astronomical Data
arxiv-1905-13189.creator: Markus Pössel Haus der Astronomie and Max Planck Institute for Astronomy
arxiv-1905-13189.description: Abstract 1 Introduction Compare professional astronomy today with how it was 50 years ago, and you will recognise some continuity — but also a number of fundamental changes. Perhaps the key change is that astronomy has come to rely almost completely on digital data.

arxiv-2105-02722.title: Mutual Visibility in Graphs
arxiv-2105-02722.creator: Gabriele Di Stefano
arxiv-2105-02722.description: Abstract Let G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) be a graph and P ⊆ V P\subseteq V a set of points . Two points are mutually visible if there is a shortest path between them without further points. P P is a mutual-visibility set if its points are pairwise mutually visible.

arxiv-2106-07083.title: Hamiltonicity of 3-tough ( K 2 ∪ 3 ​ K 1 ) (K_{2}\cup 3K_{1}) -free graphs
arxiv-2106-07083.creator: Elizabeth Grimm, Andrew Hatfield
arxiv-2106-07083.description: Abstract Chvátal conjectured in 1973 the existence of some constant t t such that all t t -tough graphs with at least three vertices are hamiltonian. While the conjecture has been proven for some special classes of graphs, it remains open in general.

arxiv-2107-09567.title: SiO masers and 7 mm continuum emission in binary AGB stars Mira and R Aqr.
arxiv-2107-09567.creator: W. D. Cotton, E. Humphreys, M. Wittkowski, A. Baudry, A. M. S. Richards, W. Vlemmings, T. Khouri, S. Etoka
arxiv-2107-09567.description: Abstract Interactions between AGB stars and a secondary in a close orbit are one possible explanation of why some AGB stars develop into aspherical planetary nebulae. This study uses millimeter observations of the continuum and SiO maser emission in several symbiotic Miras looking for evidence of an interaction between the two stars.

arxiv-2202-06555.title: High-Dimensional Dynamic Stochastic Model Representation Thanks: Submitted to the editors on January 6, 2021.
arxiv-2202-06555.creator: Aryan Eftekhari, Simon Scheidegger
arxiv-2202-06555.description: Abstract We propose a scalable method for computing global solutions of nonlinear, high-dimensional dynamic stochastic economic models. First, within a time iteration framework, we approximate economic policy functions using an adaptive, high-dimensional model representation scheme, combined with adaptive sparse grids to address the ubiquitous challenge of the curse of dimensionality.

arxiv-2204-01053.title: Quantum backaction effects in sequential measurements
arxiv-2204-01053.creator: Le Bin Ho
arxiv-2204-01053.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Le Bin Ho. Quantum backaction refers to the disturbance of a quantum system caused by measuring it. In sequential measurements, this effect can accumulate and become significant, leading to nontrivial modifications of the system state and the measurement results. This paper explores the ways in which quantum backaction can manifest in sequential measurements, including the role of measurement strength and the nature of the measurement process. The paper highlights the insight quantum foundation and the implications for quantum measurement and information processing.

arxiv-2303-10291.title: Detection of Uncertainty in Exceedance of Threshold (DUET): An Adversarial Patch Localizer
arxiv-2303-10291.creator: Terence Jie Chua 1 , Wenhan Yu 1 , Chang Liu 1 , and Jun Zhao 2
arxiv-2303-10291.description: Abstract Development of defenses against physical world attacks such as adversarial patches is gaining traction within the research community. We contribute to the field of adversarial patch detection by introducing an uncertainty-based adversarial patch localizer which localizes adversarial patch on an image, permitting post-processing patch-avoidance or patch-reconstruction.

arxiv-2303-11007.title: Simple experimental realization of optical Hilbert Hotel using scalar and vector fractional vortex beams
arxiv-2303-11007.creator: Subith Kumar, Anirban Ghosh, Chahat Kaushik, Arash Shiri, Greg Gbur, Sudhir Sharma, G. K. Samanta
arxiv-2303-11007.description: Abstract Historically, infinity was long considered a vague concept – boundless, endless, larger than the largest – without any quantifiable mathematical foundation. This view changed in the 1800s through the pioneering work of Georg Cantor showing that infinite sets follow their own seemingly paradoxical mathematical rules.

arxiv-2305-16978.title: Meandering Microstrip Leaky-Wave Antenna with Dual-band Linear–Circular Polarization and Suppressed Open Stopband
arxiv-2305-16978.creator: Pratik Vadher, Giulia Sacco, and Denys Nikolayev
arxiv-2305-16978.description: Abstract This paper proposes a dual-band frequency scanning meandering microstrip leaky-wave antenna with linear polarization in the Ku-band and circular polarization in the K-band. This is achieved by making use of two spatial harmonics for radiation. The unit cell of the periodic microstrip antenna contains three meanders with mitred corners.

arxiv-2309-10859.title: Systematics in the Cepheid and TRGB Distance Scales: Metallicity Sensitivity of the Wesenheit Leavitt Law
arxiv-2309-10859.creator: Barry F. Madore, Wendy L. Freedman
arxiv-2309-10859.description: Abstract Using an updated and significantly augmented sample of Cepheid and TRGB distances to 28 nearby spiral and irregular galaxies, covering a wide range of metallicities, we have searched for evidence of a correlation of the zero-point of the Cepheid Period-Luminosity relation with HII region (gas-phase) metallicities. Our analysis, for the 21 galaxies closer than 12.

arxiv-2412-10553.title: Edge AI-based Radio Frequency Fingerprinting for IoT Networks This paper was produced by the IEEE Publication Technology Group. They are in Piscataway, NJ. Manuscript received December 2024.
arxiv-2412-10553.creator: Ahmed Mohamed Hussain 1 , Nada Abughanam 2 , and Panos Papadimitratos 1
arxiv-2412-10553.description: Abstract The deployment of the Internet of Things (IoT) in smart cities and critical infrastructure has enhanced connectivity and real-time data exchange but introduced significant security challenges. While effective, cryptography can often be resource-intensive for small-footprint resource-constrained (i.e., IoT) devices.

arxiv-2501-06601.title: On certain integral Frobenius period maps for Shimura varieties and their reductions
arxiv-2501-06601.creator: Qijun Yan
arxiv-2501-06601.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Qijun Yan. We formulate an integral Frobenius period map for the framed crystalline prismatization of the p p -integral model 𝒮 \mathcal{S} of a Shimura variety with good reduction. By analyzing reductions of this map, we derive a period map from the mod p p fiber S S of 𝒮 \mathcal{S} to the moduli stack of 1-1 truncated local G G -shtukas in the prismatic topology, which refines the zip period map of S S within this topology.

arxiv-2512-24348.title: An explicit construction of heat kernels and Green’s functions in measure spaces
arxiv-2512-24348.creator: Palle Jorgensen and Jay Jorgenson and Lejla Smajlović
arxiv-2512-24348.description: Abstract . We explicitly construct a heat kernel as a Neumann series for certain function spaces, such as L 1 L^{1} , L 2 L^{2} , and Hilbert spaces, associated to a locally compact Hausdorff space 𝔛 \mathfrak{X} with Borel σ \sigma -algebra ℬ \mathcal{B} , and endowed with additional measure-theoretic data.

arxiv-2606-05125.title: Experimentally probing the Quantum Physics in the Inverted Harmonic Oscillator
arxiv-2606-05125.creator: Si-Cong Ji, Philipp Schüttelkopf, Nataliia Bazhan, Federica Cataldini, Mohammadamin Tajik, Frederik S. Møller, Igor Mazets, Sebastian Erne, Jörg Schmiedmayer

frus-1863p1-d224.title: Mr. Seward to Mr. Adams.
frus-1863p1-d224.creator: U.S. Department of State
frus-1863p1-d224.source: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
frus-1863p1-d224.description: FRUS Papers Relating to Foreign Affairs, Accompanying the Annual Message of the Presi, Document 224, dated 29 June 1863: Mr. Seward to Mr. Adams.

pmc-10614653.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Sub-Lineage 4.2.2/SIT149 as Dominant Drug-Resistant Clade in Northwest Ethiopia 2020–2022: In-silico Whole-Genome Sequence Analysis
pmc-10614653.creator: Daniel Mekonnen, Abaineh Munshea, Endalkachew Nibret, Bethlehem Adnew, Hailu Getachew, Amiro Kebede, Ananya Gebrewahid, Silvia Herrera-Leon, Aranzazu Amor Aramendia, Agustín Benito, Estefanía Abascal, Camille Jacqueline, Abraham Aseffa, Laura Herrera-Leon
pmc-10614653.description: IntroductionDrug resistance (DR) in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) is mainly associated with certain lineages and varies across regions and countries. The Beijing genotype is the leading resistant lineage in Asia and western countries. M. tuberculosis (Mtb) (sub) lineages responsible for most drug resistance in Ethiopia are not well described.

pmc-10696721.title: Plasmodium yoelii iron transporter PyDMT1 interacts with host ferritin and is required in full activity for malarial pathogenesis
pmc-10696721.creator: Mengjiao Zhong, Bing Zhou
pmc-10696721.description: BackgroundThe rapid reproduction of malaria parasites requires proper iron uptake. However, the process of iron absorption by parasites is rarely studied. Divalent metal transporter (DMT1) is a critical iron transporter responsible for uptaking iron. A homolog of human DMT1 exists in the malaria parasite genome, which in Plasmodium yoelii is hereafter named PyDMT1.ResultsPyDMT1 knockout appears to be lethal.

pmc-11413978.title: Snapshot of Examination Usage in Emergency Medicine Clerkships
pmc-11413978.creator: William D Alley, Iltifat Husain, Blake Briggs, David Story
pmc-11413978.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveEmergency Medicine (EM) clerkships often use a written exam to assess the knowledge gained over the course of an EM rotation in medical school. Clerkship Directors (CDs) may choose the National Board of Medical Examiners (NBME) EM Advanced Clinical Science Subject Exam (ACE), the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine (SAEM) M4 exam, which has two versions, the SAEM M3 exam, or departmental exams. There are currently no published guidelines or consensus regarding their utility.

pmc-11516457.title: Forced displacement and the healthcare workforce crisis: Venezuelan healthcare workers in Peru
pmc-11516457.creator: G Rees
pmc-11516457.description: BackgroundThe migration of healthcare workforces tends to be economically based benefiting high income countries, while draining lower-income countries of workers and skills. However, national instability or civil conflict may also have the effect of forcing out health workers. Few articles focus on the experiences of these types of migrants.

pmc-11542658.title: High-transmission spectrometer for rapid resonant inelastic soft X-ray scattering (rRIXS) maps
pmc-11542658.creator: Lothar Weinhardt, Constantin Wansorra, Ralph Steininger, Thomas Spangenberg, Dirk Hauschild, Clemens Heske
pmc-11542658.description: A high-transmission soft X-ray spectrometer has been developed and commissioned at the X-SPEC beamline of the KIT Light Source. With this spectrometer, single spectra can be measured with exposure times well below 1 s, allowing the rapid collection of full resonant inelastic soft X-ray scattering maps in less than one minute.

pmc-11862196.title: Peculiarities of social functioning in patients with negative symptoms in schizophrenia
pmc-11862196.creator: N O Maruta, Y A Kushnir, G Y Kalenska
pmc-11862196.description: IntroductionThe prevalence of schizophrenia in the world is between 0.4 and 1.4%, and the number of patients with negative symptoms (NS) in this group reaches 90%. NS are considered key components of schizophrenia that negatively affect social functioning (SF) and quality of life in patients with schizophrenia.

pmc-12471375.title: The Link Between Oxidative Stress and Male Infertility in Lithuania: A Retrospective Study
pmc-12471375.creator: Eglė Jašinskienė, Marija Čaplinskienė
pmc-12471375.description: Background and Objectives: Male infertility is a growing public health concern, with up to 50% of cases lacking a clearly identifiable cause. This study aimed to assess the epidemiological characteristics of male infertility in Lithuania and evaluate the clinical utility of oxidative stress assessment using the MiOXSYS system.

pmc-12501087.title: Intrarenal venous flow patterns and their association with successful fluid removal in critically ill patients: a prospective observational exploratory study
pmc-12501087.creator: Chailat Maluangnon, Apatsara Saokaew, Satit Rojwatcharapibarn, Ranistha Ratanarat
pmc-12501087.description: BackgroundDetermining the optimal timing for fluid removal in critically ill patients remains a challenge. This study evaluated the utility of Doppler ultrasound, specifically intrarenal venous flow (IRVF) patterns and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) scores, and their associations with fluid removal outcomes, hemodynamic parameters, and clinical endpoints.

pmc-12509410.title: Recent advances in immunological mechanisms and murine disease models of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies
pmc-12509410.creator: Akiko Nishidate, Mariam Piruzyan, Manami Kikuchi, Yuzo Koda
pmc-12509410.description: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) are a group of autoimmune muscle disorders characterized by muscle weakness caused by muscle tissue inflammation, as well as lung and skin symptoms. Their pathophysiology and exacerbation are primarily associated with the tissue infiltration of immune cells, such as T cells and macrophages, revealing a strong connection with the immune system.

pmc-12562790.title: Clinical and economic burden of herpes zoster in Mexico: A retrospective medical chart analysis in a private healthcare setting
pmc-12562790.creator: Nurilign Ahmed, Adriana Guzman-Holst, Gloria Huerta-Garcia, Edgar Perez Barragan, Francisco Marquez-Díaz, Alejandro E Macías, Adrian Camacho-Ortiz, Juan Carlos Tinoco
pmc-12562790.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Herpes zoster (HZ) is characterized by a unilateral, painful rash, which in most cases requires medical attention and pharmacological treatment. Several complications, including postherpetic neuralgia (PHN), may increase the burden of illness and healthcare costs. The objective of this study was to evaluate healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), and direct and indirect costs incurred by patients with HZ from a private sector perspective in Mexico.

pmc-12579857.title: Protective Effects of Irisin Against LPS-Induced Intestinal Injury and Its Influence on Gut Microbiota in Septic Mice
pmc-12579857.creator: Ling Yang, Mudi Liu, Beilin Hu, Kangle Yong, Jun Zhou, Ye Chen
pmc-12579857.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIrisin, a novel myokine, has garnered significant attention for its roles in metabolic regulation and anti-inflammatory responses. Sepsis disrupts the intestinal microenvironment, exacerbating its progression and highlighting the need for novel therapeutic approaches.

pmc-12700543.title: IL-17–producing γδ T cells in the tumor microenvironment promote radioresistance in mice
pmc-12700543.creator: Yue Deng, Xixi Liu, Xiao Yang, Wenwen Wei, Jiacheng Wang, Zheng Yang, Yajie Sun, Yan Hu, Haibo Zhang, Yijun Wang, Zhanjie Zhang, Lu Wen, Fang Huang, Kunyu Yang, Chao Wan
pmc-12700543.description: The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) drives radioresistance, but the role of γδ T cells in regulating radiosensitivity remains incompletely understood. In this study, we found that γδ T cell infiltration in the TME substantially increased after radiotherapy and contributed to radioresistance. Depletion of γδ T cells enhanced radiosensitivity.

pmc-12705669.title: Histone methyltransferase PRDM9 promotes survival of drug-tolerant persister cells in glioblastoma
pmc-12705669.creator: George L Joun, Emma G Kempe, Brianna Chen, Jayden R Sterling, Ramzi H Abbassi, Dana Friess, Matthew Singleton, Chandra Choudhury, Oana C Marian, W Daniel du Preez, Ariadna Recasens, Teleri Clark, Tian Y Du, Jason K K Low, Hani Kim, Pengyi Yang, Jasmine Khor, Monira Hoque, Dinesh C Indurthi, Mani Kuc
pmc-12705669.description: Chemotherapy often kills a large fraction of cancer cells but leaves behind a small population of drug-tolerant persister cells. These persister cells survive drug treatments through reversible, non-genetic mechanisms and cause tumour recurrence upon cessation of therapy. Here, we report a drug tolerance mechanism regulated by the germ-cell-specific H3K4 methyltransferase PRDM9.

pmc-13155087.title: Reply – RE: Policy Versus Practice: Facilitators and Barriers of Chronic Care Integration in Dutch General Practice – a Survey Study
pmc-13155087.creator: Toine E. P. Remers, Simone A. Van Dulmen, Erik W. M. A. Bischoff, Florien M. Kruse, Marcel G. M. Olde Rikkert, Patrick P. T. Jeurissen
pmc-13155087.description: r work. While we understand the nuance raised by the author(s) regarding the interpretation of our survey results, we would like to emphasize that this is primarily a matter of perspective and that we made a deliberate and carefully considered choice in how we reported these findings.

pmc-13183509.title: Arterial supplies to the spleen in the rat (Rattus norvegicus), degu (Octodon degus), and red-bellied squirrel (Callosciurus erythraeus)
pmc-13183509.creator: Tetsuhito KIGATA, Yuine WATANABE, Mio MATSUURA, Keiko SAKAI
pmc-13183509.description: Rodents exhibit diverse morphological and ecological adaptations across species, making them important species for considering the evolutionary background of morphological traits. Although the splenic artery has been described in various rodent species, interspecific comparisons remain difficult due to a lack of uniformity in anatomical descriptions.

pmc-13192406.title: Effect of feeding increasing concentrations of rumen-protected carbohydrate on the growth performance and blood and plasma metabolites of receiving feedlot heifers
pmc-13192406.creator: J P Russi, Nicolas DiLorenzo, Alejandro E Relling
pmc-13192406.description: The objective of this experiment was to evaluate the inclusion of a rumen-protected carbohydrate (RPC) on growth performance and plasma metabolites in growing beef heifers. Crossbred heifers (n = 135; 136 ± 14 kg) were used in a 63-d experiment.

pmc-13290636.title: Impact of rehabilitation trajectory on affective and cognitive impairment after intracerebral hemorrhage: a cohort study
pmc-13290636.creator: Qiuyi Jiang, Guangyao Shi, Hongli Zhang, Shouyue Wu, Chunyang Liu, Jian Zhang, Enzhou Lu, Chao Yuan, Yanchao Liang, Lu Wang, Guang Yang

pmc-13337247.title: Single‐Cell Transcriptomics and Development of Gametocyte‐Specific Molecular Markers for Avian Malaria Parasites
pmc-13337247.creator: A Berthomieu, I Rizos, J W Bagnoli, S Gandon, A M Talman, A Rivero
pmc-13337247.description: Avian malaria, caused by Plasmodium parasites, poses a significant threat to bird populations worldwide, particularly in vulnerable island ecosystems. Yet, progress in understanding avian malaria transmission dynamics has been hampered by the lack of molecular tools to quantify and sex the transmissible stages of the parasite: the male and female gametocytes.

pmc-13473237.title: Alternative Polyadenylation in the Brain is Modulated by Chronic Ethanol Exposure in a Sex- and Cell Type–Specific Manner
pmc-13473237.creator: Petar N Grozdanov, Laura B Ferguson, Brent R Kisby, Clinton C MacDonald, Robert O Messing, Igor Ponomarev
pmc-13473237.description: Alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a common posttranscriptional mechanism to regulate gene expression. APA generates mRNA isoforms that differ in 3′ UTR length or, through alternative last exons, encode distinct protein carboxyl termini. This is especially consequential in neurons, where these isoforms are often asymmetrically localized to dendrites and axons and can be locally translated.

pmc-13474481.title: From brain circuits to self-regulation: an integrative neurocognitive model of metacognition and emotion regulation in ADHD
pmc-13474481.creator: Davoud Amiri, Lamberto Briziarelli, Swetang J. Shah, Sara Amiri, Amin Vakili, Amir Hossein Jalali Nadoushan

pmc-13570914.title: Association of three different dietary patterns with the metabolomic profiles of children: the BiomarKid project
pmc-13570914.creator: Irina Gheorghita, Lara Vehovec, Veit Grote, Jeannie Horak, Mariona Gispert-Llauradó, Natalia Ferré, Berthold Koletzko, Hans Demmelmair, Klaus Kratochwill, Elvira Verduci, Dariusz Gruszfeld, Joaquin Escribano, Gabi Kastenmüller, Veronica Luque
pmc-13570914.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and aimsMetabolomics offers a promising approach to objectively assess food intake and nutrition-related health risks. Three different dietary patterns (DPs) associated with cardiometabolic health were previously identified at 2 years of age in the EU Childhood Obesity Project and were used as reference patterns for longitudinal scoring throughout childhood: “Core foods” DP (CORE), rich in vegetables, fruits, fish, meat, and olive oil; “Animal protein sources” DP (PROT), high in white meat, processed meat, flavoured milk, snacks, fish, and vegetables; and “Poor-quality

pmc-13584948.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Gut Microbiota and Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Research Trends and Frontiers
pmc-13584948.creator: Chengpu Zhao, Xiangcheng Hu
pmc-13584948.description: BackgroundThe gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) pathogenesis via the gut-liver axis. Existing gut microbiota-HCC studies are mostly narrative, with three critical knowledge gaps: lack of data-driven global research mapping, unclear staged field evolution, and insufficient quantitative identification of research frontiers.

pmc-13670418.title: Co‐Design of the MAGNET Intervention to Enhance Medicines Self‐Management in Community‐Dwelling People With Dementia and Their Family Carers
pmc-13670418.creator: Catherine Powell, Lubena Mirza, Mohammed Akhlak Rauf, Justine Tomlinson, Zoe Edwards, Rozeena Khan, Jan Speechley, John L O'Dwyer, Catherine Quinn, Beth Fylan
pmc-13670418.description: BackgroundWith appropriate support people living with mild‐moderate dementia and family carers can self‐manage their medicines. However, existing interventions often focus on enhancing adherence to a medication regimen rather than supporting people with other areas, such as monitoring side effects or checking for errors.
